info.title: Zahln Mensa API
info.description:
The API behind the Zahln mensa payment flow, for the frontend take-home.

A cashier rings up an order on the till, and the till shows `qrPayload` as a QR code. The QR names the order, not an amount, because the price depends on who pays: students, staff and guests pay different prices for the same dish. A payer scans the QR, reads the order with `GET /orders/{orderId}` (which shows the amount for their price group), and pays it with `POST /orders/{orderId}/payments`. The till polls `GET /orders/{orderId}` until the order is `paid`. The finance team reads payments and daily totals.

## Your candidate ID

Send `X-Candidate-Id` on every request. Your data is separate from everyone else's. The server starts you with seeded data: 3 mensas, 6 tills and 30 days of payments.

## Seeded logins

All passwords are `test1234`.

| Username | Role | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `student`, `staff`, `guest` | payer | Student app. The same order costs a different amount for each. |
| `cashier-campus-1`, `cashier-campus-2`, `cashier-campus-3` | cashier | Till at Mensa am Campus |
| `cashier-nord-1`, `cashier-nord-2` | cashier | Till at Mensa Nord |
| `cashier-bibliothek-1` | cashier | Till at Cafeteria Bibliothek |
| `finance` | finance | Studierendenwerk dashboard |

## How the server behaves

It behaves like production on a campus network. Build for this:

- **Slow and failing requests.** Requests can take seconds. They can fail with `503 unavailable` before anything happens.
- **Lost responses.** A request can be handled and its change saved, and the client still gets `504 timeout`, `502 connection_dropped` or no response at all. The outcome is unknown until you check.
- **Idempotency.** Every POST that changes money or orders needs an `Idempotency-Key` header. Use one key per intent and reuse it for every retry of that intent. A repeat returns the original result with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. The same key with a different body is refused with `422 idempotency_mismatch`. Keys are kept for 24 hours, per user.
- **Out-of-date reads.** A GET can return an earlier state of the same resource. Orders and payments carry `version`, which only grows. Never replace what you show with a lower version.
- **Sessions end.** An access token lasts 5 minutes and can end sooner. On `401 session_expired`, log in again and retry.
- **Payments are checked.** A payment starts `pending`. It usually becomes `confirmed` or `declined` within seconds, and sometimes stays `pending` for minutes. Only `confirmed` means the payer has paid. A declined payment frees the order for another try.
- **Time.** Orders expire 5 minutes after they are made. Use the `Date` response header as the server time, not the device clock.
- **Errors** are `application/problem+json` with a stable `code` and `retryable`.

## Money

Amounts are integer cents in EUR.

post.description:
Pays the order for the logged-in student, staff member or guest. The new payment is `pending` while it is checked, usually for a few seconds and sometimes for minutes; poll `GET /payments/{paymentId}` or `GET /orders/{orderId}` for the outcome.

**Retry with the same Idempotency-Key.** A payment can be recorded even when the response is lost (timeout, 502, 504, dropped connection). Retrying with the same key returns the original payment with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`; it never pays twice. A new key for the same order is refused while a payment is pending or after it is paid.

Send `X-App-Version` from the app; a version below `minAppVersion` is refused with 426.

post.summary: Refund a payment in full or in part (cashier)
post.description: Only a cashier of the till the payment was made at can refund it. The payment must be `confirmed` and less than 30 days old, and all refunds together may not exceed it (pending refunds count). The refund starts `pending` and becomes `completed` or `failed` within seconds. Retry with the same Idempotency-Key; a new key is a new refund.
